fixer.summary: actions.study now checks that a named creature_type is one of the 14 SRD types before looking up its skill. Any other name (such as 'goblinoid') now gets a clean Refusal citing page=179, rule=GLOSS.creature-type#3 and ruling R-39, and no action is spent or check rolled. Before, it raised a KeyError. The fix also makes T-92's test pass (a session `study` command naming 'dwarf' as a type), because it goes through the same function. Unit tests, the ticket's tests with --runxfail, ruff and dev-gate all pass.

review.summary: I'm approving this. Study now checks the named creature type against CREATURE_TYPE_SKILL before it looks the type up. That table is the engine's only list of creature types, and it holds exactly the 14 from the SRD. Any other type (goblinoid, dwarf) is now refused cleanly with page=179, rule=GLOSS.creature-type#3 and ruling=R-39, which is what R-39 says to do, so the KeyError no longer happens. The new check uses the existing table, so it adds no second mechanism and no special case. The diff also removes the strict xfail markers for both T-91 and T-92. That is necessary: the same fix makes T-92's test pass too, and a strict xfail on a passing test fails the run. All 10 creature-type acceptance tests pass. The unit tests check what the code does: the refusal's citations, that no d20 is rolled for a refused Study, and that a listed type still uses its own skill.
